segments.text: The following report grew out of a 10-week program in engineering systems design held at Stanford University and the Ames Research Center of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration during the summer of 1975.
segments.search_text: The following report grew out of a 10-week program in engineering systems design held at Stanford University and the Ames Research Center of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration during the summer of 1975.

segments.text: This program, sponsored jointly by NASA and the American Society for Engineering Education, brought together nineteen professors of engineering, physical science, social science, and architecture, three volunteers, six students, a technical director, and two co-directors.
segments.search_text: This program, sponsored jointly by NASA and the American Society for Engineering Education, brought together nineteen professors of engineering, physical science, social science, and architecture, three volunteers, six students, a technical director, and two co-directors.

segments.text: This group worked for ten weeks to construct a convincing picture of how people might permanently sustain life in space on a large scale.

segments.text: This report, like the design itself, is intended to be as technologically complete and sound as it could be made in ten weeks, but it is also meant for a readership beyond that of the aerospace community.

segments.text: Because the idea of colonizing space has awakened strong public interest, the report is written to be understood by the educated public and specialists in other fields.

segments.text: The principal material resources of space are the planets, their moons, and asteroids.
segments.search_text: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Sources of Matter in Space The principal material resources of space are the planets, their moons, and asteroids.
segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Sources of Matter in Space

segments.text: Their accessibility is determined by distance from possible users of the material and by the depth of the gravitational wells through which the matter must be lifted.

segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Sources of Matter in Space

segments.text: The planets of the solar system are major loci of material resources, but they are mostly very distant from prospective colonies, and all sit at the bottoms of deep gravitational wells.

segments.text: The effort to haul material off the planets is so great as to make the other sources seem more attractive.

segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Sources of Matter in Space

segments.text: Of course, if a planet is nearby and is rich in resources, a colony might find the effort justified.

segments.text: Both the Sun and the Galaxy contribute fluxes of ionizing particles.

segments.text: The quiescent Sun constantly emits a solar wind (ref. 15) of about 5 to 10 protons, electrons, and particles per cubic centimeter traveling at speeds of about 500 km/s.
segments.search_text: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat The quiescent Sun constantly emits a solar wind (ref. 15) of about 5 to 10 protons, electrons, and particles per cubic centimeter traveling at speeds of about 500 km/s.
segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat

segments.text: These particles do not possess penetrating energies and therefore offer no threat to humans.
segments.search_text: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat These particles do not possess penetrating energies and therefore offer no threat to humans.
segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat

segments.text: However, the solar wind may indirectly affect humans because it neutralizes any separation of electric charge that might occur in space and produces a small variable interplanetary magnetic field (~5 nT at the distance of the Earth (lAU) from the Sun).
segments.search_text: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat However, the solar wind may indirectly affect humans because it neutralizes any separation of electric charge that might occur in space and produces a small variable interplanetary magnetic field (~5 nT at the distance of the Earth (lAU) from the Sun).
segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat

segments.text: Consequently, space contains essentially no electric field, whereas on Earth the electric field is 100 V /m near the surface.
segments.search_text: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat Consequently, space contains essentially no electric field, whereas on Earth the electric field is 100 V /m near the surface.
segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat

segments.text: Given that the human body is a good electrical conductor and forms an equipotential surface in the Earth's field, and that humans live a good portion of their lives in electrostatically shielded buildings, it seems unlikely that living for prolonged times in the absence of an electric field would cause harm, but this is not definitely known.

segments.heading_context: 2. Physical Properties of Space / Ionizing Radiation: Major Threat

segments.text: Similarly, although there is evidence that living in magnetic fields thousands of times more intense than the Earth's will harm people, the consequences of living in a magnetic field that is both 10,000 times weaker and variable with time are not known (refs. 16,17).

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Although several other gases have been used for this purpose, there are several reasons why nitrogen appears the most reasonable candidate for the colony.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough Although several other gases have been used for this purpose, there are several reasons why nitrogen appears the most reasonable candidate for the colony.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: For example, since nitrogen constitutes almost 80 percent of the Earth's atmosphere, it is not surprising to find that some organisms require the gas for normal development (ref. 31).
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough For example, since nitrogen constitutes almost 80 percent of the Earth's atmosphere, it is not surprising to find that some organisms require the gas for normal development (ref. 31).
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Further, with time, denitrifying bacteria will release nitrogen gas into the atmosphere, thereby resulting in the eventual accumulation of significant quantities.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough Further, with time, denitrifying bacteria will release nitrogen gas into the atmosphere, thereby resulting in the eventual accumulation of significant quantities.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Finally, the inclusion of nitrogen-fixing plants in the colony's life support system means that the gas level can be biologically maintained by the conversion of nitrogen gas into protein.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough Finally, the inclusion of nitrogen-fixing plants in the colony's life support system means that the gas level can be biologically maintained by the conversion of nitrogen gas into protein.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Thus the inevitable presence and the various benefits of nitrogen gas dictate its inclusion in the atmosphere, perhaps at a level of 26.7 kPa (~200 mm Hg).
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough Thus the inevitable presence and the various benefits of nitrogen gas dictate its inclusion in the atmosphere, perhaps at a level of 26.7 kPa (~200 mm Hg).
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: The level of carbon dioxide should be maintained below the OSHA standard (ref. 32), which specifies that pC02 be less than 0.4 kPa (3 mm Hg).
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough The level of carbon dioxide should be maintained below the OSHA standard (ref. 32), which specifies that pC02 be less than 0.4 kPa (3 mm Hg).
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: At the same time the CO₂ levels will be high enough to permit maximum rates of photosynthesis by crop plants.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough At the same time the CO₂ levels will be high enough to permit maximum rates of photosynthesis by crop plants.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Trace contaminants should be monitored and controlled to very low levels.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Finally, it is desirable to maintain a comfortable relative humidity and temperature.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough Finally, it is desirable to maintain a comfortable relative humidity and temperature.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Atmosphere: Less Is Enough

segments.text: Various sources (ref. 30) suggest a range of temperatures around 22° C and a relative humidity of about 40 percent.

segments.text: Diversity and Variability
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability Diversity and Variability
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: Environmental psychologists and behavioral scientists (refs. 37-39) have pointed out that variety, diversity, flexibility and motivation can make apparently deficient environments quite satisfactory to their inhabitants.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability Environmental psychologists and behavioral scientists (refs. 37-39) have pointed out that variety, diversity, flexibility and motivation can make apparently deficient environments quite satisfactory to their inhabitants.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: It is important that space colonists become meaningfully involved in their environment.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability It is important that space colonists become meaningfully involved in their environment.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: This can result from there being a planned complexity and ambiguity (ref. 38), that is, the design of the habitat must not be so complete as to be sterile; it must avoid motel banality.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability This can result from there being a planned complexity and ambiguity (ref. 38), that is, the design of the habitat must not be so complete as to be sterile; it must avoid motel banality.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: The ideal is to build a setting that provides individuals and groups alternate ways of satisfying their goals, thus giving them freedom of choice.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability The ideal is to build a setting that provides individuals and groups alternate ways of satisfying their goals, thus giving them freedom of choice.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: Attaining such an ideal is greatly facilitated by the large size of the habitat which frees from limitations planned for in the small interiors of space stations.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability Attaining such an ideal is greatly facilitated by the large size of the habitat which frees from limitations planned for in the small interiors of space stations.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: In particular the interior should have a general plan so that the finishing and details can be left to the choice of the colonists themselves.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability In particular the interior should have a general plan so that the finishing and details can be left to the choice of the colonists themselves.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: Emphasis in the design of living area of a space colony should not be on specifics, but on the range of options.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability Emphasis in the design of living area of a space colony should not be on specifics, but on the range of options.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: Colonists need access to both large and small, private and community spaces, to long vistas and short ones, but with a flexible, manipulatable architecture.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability Colonists need access to both large and small, private and community spaces, to long vistas and short ones, but with a flexible, manipulatable architecture.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: They need to be able to exploit and to change these spaces according to individual wants.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability They need to be able to exploit and to change these spaces according to individual wants.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: The initial design must permit the colonists to reshape the interior by developing and altering the spaces.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability The initial design must permit the colonists to reshape the interior by developing and altering the spaces.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: To these ends a building system must be developed which is fairly flexible, light weight, easily mass produced, capable of fast efficient erection, and yet allows a variety of spaces to evolve.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability To these ends a building system must be developed which is fairly flexible, light weight, easily mass produced, capable of fast efficient erection, and yet allows a variety of spaces to evolve.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: It must also provide a sufficient esthetic quality, both materially and spatially.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability It must also provide a sufficient esthetic quality, both materially and spatially.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: These criteria suggest a system that is built from modular components; that is, panels and structural elements that are uniform in size but when stacked or laid horizontally allow any combinations of shapes to be achieved.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability These criteria suggest a system that is built from modular components; that is, panels and structural elements that are uniform in size but when stacked or laid horizontally allow any combinations of shapes to be achieved.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Diversity and Variability

segments.text: It then exaggerates the sense of artificiality, although it is possible to represent the natural environment by miniature design with a high degree of perfection and satisfaction, as in Japanese gardens.

segments.text: To design a human habitation in space, a criterion must be set for area available, most conveniently expressed in terms of area per person.

segments.text: The amount of area allocated per person has two important consequences: it determines the population density of habitation on which depends the sense of crowding; it limits services and facilities provided to the inhabitants.

segments.text: The organizational criteria have to do with both physical organization and social and managerial organization.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Organizational Criteria

segments.text: In the first category is the criterion that the components of the colony be located so that the resources of space can be effectively exploited: solar energy, matter in the Moon or asteroids and on Earth, high vacuum of space and possibilities of pseudogravity variable from 0 g to more than 1 g.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Organizational Criteria

segments.text: The colony must be provided with a transportation system that is capable of sustaining close contact with Earth, and with extensive electronic communications.

segments.text: Nevertheless, the organization must be such as to permit comfortable life under crowded conditions far from other human communities.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Organizational Criteria

segments.text: Solipsism is a philosophical theory that everything is in the imagination, and there is no reality outside one's own brain.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: As a philosophical theory it is interesting because is is internally consistent and, therefore, cannot be disproved.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: But as a psycholOgical state, it is highly uncomfortable.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment But as a psycholOgical state, it is highly uncomfortable.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: The whole of life becomes a long dream from which an individual can never wake up. Each person is trapped in a nightmare.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment The whole of life becomes a long dream from which an individual can never wake up. Each person is trapped in a nightmare.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: Even friends are not real, they are a part of the dream.

segments.text: A person feels very lonely and detached, and eventually becomes apathetic and indifferent.

segments.text: In the small town of Lund, Sweden, the winter days have 6 hr of daylight and 18 hr of darkness.

segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: Most of the time people live under artificial light, so that life acquires a special quality.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment Most of the time people live under artificial light, so that life acquires a special quality.

segments.text: Outdoors, there is no landscape to see; only street corners lit by lamps.

segments.text: There are several means to alleviate the tendency toward the solipsism syndrome in the extra terrestrial communities:
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment There are several means to alleviate the tendency toward the solipsism syndrome in the extra terrestrial communities:
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: A large geometry, in which people can see far beyond the "theater stage" of the vicinity to a view which is overwhelmingly visible.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment A large geometry, in which people can see far beyond the "theater stage" of the vicinity to a view which is overwhelmingly visible.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / The Solipsism Syndrome in Artificial Environment

segments.text: Something'must exist beyond each human's manipulation because people learn to cope with reality when reality is different from their imagination. If the reality is the same as the imagination, there is no escape from falling into solipsism. In extraterrestrial communities, everything can be virtually controlled. In fact, technically nothing should go beyond human control even though this is psychologically bad. However, some amount of "unpredictability" can be built in within a controllable range. One way to achieve this is to generate artificial unpredictability by means of a table of random numbers. Another way is to allow animals and plants a degree of freedom and independence from human planning. Both types of unpredictability must have a high visibility to be effective. This high visibility is easier to achieve in a macrogeometry which allows longer lines of sight.

segments.text: Something must exist which grows. Interactive processes generate new patterns which cannot be inferred from the information contained in the old state. This is not due to randomness but rather to different amplification by mutual causal loops. It is important for each person to feel able to contribute personally to something which grows, that the reality often goes in a direction different from expectation, and finally that what each person takes care of (a child, for example) may possess increased wisdom, and may grow into something beyond the individual in control. From this point of view, it is important personally to raise children, and to grow vegetables and trees with personal care, not by mechanical means. It is also desirable to see plants and animals grow, which is facilitated by a long line of sight.

segments.text: Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic

segments.text: People in this community believe that if there are many ways, there must be the best way among them, and that the "best way" is "good" for everybody.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic People in this community believe that if there are many ways, there must be the best way among them, and that the "best way" is "good" for everybody.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic

segments.text: They think in terms of maximization and optimization.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic They think in terms of maximization and optimization.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic

segments.text: They consider majority rule as the basis of democracy, and competition as the basis of "progress." They look for universal criteria and universal categories which would apply to all people, and they look for unity by means of similarities.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic They consider majority rule as the basis of democracy, and competition as the basis of "progress." They look for universal criteria and universal categories which would apply to all people, and they look for unity by means of similarities.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic

segments.text: Differences are considered as accidental, inconvenient or bothersome, and are ignored as much as possible.
segments.search_text: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic Differences are considered as accidental, inconvenient or bothersome, and are ignored as much as possible.
segments.heading_context: 3. Human Needs in Space / Type A Community: Hierarchial and Homogenistic

segments.text: Diversity, nonstandard behavior, and minority groups are considered abnormal and undesirable, to be corrected to be more "normal." If these people are inconvenienced by the system which is geared toward the majority, the fault is considered to reside in the "abnormal" people.

segments.text: Because of the belief in the "best way" for all people and in maximum efficiency, aU living units are designed alike.

segments.text: The purpose of this chapter is to answer these questions by evaluating reasonable alternatives in terms of the goals of the design study (ch. 1) and the criteria laid out in chapters 2 and 3.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives The purpose of this chapter is to answer these questions by evaluating reasonable alternatives in terms of the goals of the design study (ch. 1) and the criteria laid out in chapters 2 and 3.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives

segments.text: A successful systems design combines subsystems satisfying various conflicting criteria to produce a unified working entity.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives A successful systems design combines subsystems satisfying various conflicting criteria to produce a unified working entity.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives

segments.text: The parts of the space colony - transportation, mining, the habitat, manufacturing, agriculture, and so on - must interact and interrelate in such a way that the demands of each for energy, raw materials, manpower, transport, and waste removal can be met by the overall system.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives The parts of the space colony - transportation, mining, the habitat, manufacturing, agriculture, and so on - must interact and interrelate in such a way that the demands of each for energy, raw materials, manpower, transport, and waste removal can be met by the overall system.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives

segments.text: In turn this system must satisfy the physiological, cultural, architectural, and physical criteria necessary to maintain a permanent human community in space using near-term technology and at a minimum cost.

segments.text: In 10 weeks the study group was able to assemble only one reasonably consistent picture of life in space; there was no time to go back through the system and attempt to find optimal combinations of the subsystems. segments.text: Effort devoted to alternatives depended upon the particular subject.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives Effort devoted to alternatives depended upon the particular subject.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives

segments.text: A great deal of time was spent considering different forms for the habitat, how to handle the shielding and how to process lunar material.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives A great deal of time was spent considering different forms for the habitat, how to handle the shielding and how to process lunar material.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives

segments.text: Less time was given to considering alternative patterns of siting the colony and its parts, of different ways to achieve life support, or of various possible transportation systems. segments.text: To fulfill the criteria set forth in chapter 2, a lightweight, modular building system must be developed to serve as an enclosing means for the various spatial needs of the colony.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Structures Inside the Habitat To fulfill the criteria set forth in chapter 2, a lightweight, modular building system must be developed to serve as an enclosing means for the various spatial needs of the colony.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Structures Inside the Habitat

segments.text: Modular building systems developed on Earth can be categorized into three general types: that is, box systems using room-size modules; bearing-panel systems; and structural-frame systems. A box system entails assembling either complete shells err fully completed packages with integrated mechanical subsystems. Bearing-panel systems use load-bearing wall elements with mechanical subsystems installed during erection.

segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Structures Inside the Habitat

segments.text: Structural-frame systems use modularized framing elements in combination with nonload-bearing wall panels and mechanical subsystems which are normally installed during erection.

segments.text: A variety of alternatives exist for the processing of lunar ores to yield materials for the colony.

segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: The decision as to whether to process at the colony or on the Moon is dictated by various factors.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? The decision as to whether to process at the colony or on the Moon is dictated by various factors.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: The lunar site has the advantage of being close to the ore source and having a gravity which might be used in some chemical processing.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? The lunar site has the advantage of being close to the ore source and having a gravity which might be used in some chemical processing.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: Lunar processing might be expected to decrease the amount of material to be shipped to the colony.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? Lunar processing might be expected to decrease the amount of material to be shipped to the colony.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: However, closer examination reveals that the colony's shielding requirements exceed the slag production of the processing plant; hence, no transportation is saved by processing at a lunar site.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? However, closer examination reveals that the colony's shielding requirements exceed the slag production of the processing plant; hence, no transportation is saved by processing at a lunar site.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: Moreover, lunar processing also possesses certain definite disadvantages when compared to processing at the site of the colony.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? Moreover, lunar processing also possesses certain definite disadvantages when compared to processing at the site of the colony.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: Plant facilities shipped from the Earth to the Moon require much greater transportation expense than for shipment to the colony site.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? Plant facilities shipped from the Earth to the Moon require much greater transportation expense than for shipment to the colony site.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: In addition, solar furnaces and power plants are limited to a 50 percent duty cycle on the Moon.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where? In addition, solar furnaces and power plants are limited to a 50 percent duty cycle on the Moon.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: Without power storage this would curtail operations at a lunar processing site.

segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Processing: Where?

segments.text: The lunar gas gun is a fundamentally diffe rent concept to that of the TLA.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Appendix K — The Lunar Gas Gun Mass Driver The lunar gas gun is a fundamentally diffe rent concept to that of the TLA.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Appendix K — The Lunar Gas Gun Mass Driver

segments.text: Where the TLA launches small payloads with very high repetition rate onto a precisely determined trajectory, and has the small individ ualloads caught in a localized active net or passive catcher, the gas gun launches large payloads with a much lower repetition rate onto a less precisely determined trajectory and has these large payloads collected by remote controlled interceptor rocket engines.
segments.search_text: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Appendix K — The Lunar Gas Gun Mass Driver Where the TLA launches small payloads with very high repetition rate onto a precisely determined trajectory, and has the small individ ualloads caught in a localized active net or passive catcher, the gas gun launches large payloads with a much lower repetition rate onto a less precisely determined trajectory and has these large payloads collected by remote controlled interceptor rocket engines.
segments.heading_context: 4. Choosing Among Alternatives / Appendix K — The Lunar Gas Gun Mass Driver

segments.text: The gas gun has four primary elements in its system: a) the launching barrel on the lunar surface, b) the energy storage system which uses compressed hydrogen to propel the payload, where the propulsion energy is obtained from the hydrogen gas maintained at a pressure of 200 MPa in a blast hole deep beneath the lunar surface, c) the compressor which maintains the gas at high pressure and is driven by a nuclear turbine, and d) the interceptor rockets.

segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher The Mass Launcher
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: Critical to the success of the entire system of colonization of space is the ability to launch large amounts of matter cheaply from the Moon.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher Critical to the success of the entire system of colonization of space is the ability to launch large amounts of matter cheaply from the Moon.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: There are two aspects: launching the material from the Moon by an electromagnetic launcher using the principle of the linear induction motor, and gathering the lunar material in space by an active catcher located at L 2 •
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher There are two aspects: launching the material from the Moon by an electromagnetic launcher using the principle of the linear induction motor, and gathering the lunar material in space by an active catcher located at L 2 •
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: Each second the mass launcher accelerates five 10-kg masses of lunar material to lunar escape velocity of 2400 m/s.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher Each second the mass launcher accelerates five 10-kg masses of lunar material to lunar escape velocity of 2400 m/s.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: Errors in launch velocity are kept within 10-4 m/s along the flight path and 10-3 mls crosswise to it.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher Errors in launch velocity are kept within 10-4 m/s along the flight path and 10-3 mls crosswise to it.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: The masses are carried in an accelerating container or "bucket." Built into the walls of each bucket are liquidhelium-cooled superconducting magnets which suspend it above the track.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher The masses are carried in an accelerating container or "bucket." Built into the walls of each bucket are liquidhelium-cooled superconducting magnets which suspend it above the track.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: The buckets are accelerated at 30 g over 10k m by a linear electric motor running the length of the track.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher The buckets are accelerated at 30 g over 10k m by a linear electric motor running the length of the track.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: The bucket then enters a drift section of track, where vibrations and oscillations lose amplitude enough for the payload to be released with great precision of velocity.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher The bucket then enters a drift section of track, where vibrations and oscillations lose amplitude enough for the payload to be released with great precision of velocity.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: The velocity of each bucket is measured, and adjusted to achieve the correct value at release.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher The velocity of each bucket is measured, and adjusted to achieve the correct value at release.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: During acceleration the payload is tightly held in the bucket, but when lunar escape velocity is reached and the velocity is correct the payload is released.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher During acceleration the payload is tightly held in the bucket, but when lunar escape velocity is reached and the velocity is correct the payload is released.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: Since the bucket is constrained by the track to follow the curve of the lunar surface, the payload rises relative to the surface and proceeds into space.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher Since the bucket is constrained by the track to follow the curve of the lunar surface, the payload rises relative to the surface and proceeds into space.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: Each bucket then enters a 3 km region where a trackside linear synchronous motor decelerates it at over 100 g.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher Each bucket then enters a 3 km region where a trackside linear synchronous motor decelerates it at over 100 g.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: It is returned to the loading end of the track along a track parallel to the accelerator.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher It is returned to the loading end of the track along a track parallel to the accelerator.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / The Mass Launcher

segments.text: The structural system consists of aluminum tube columns with a typical 4 X 6 m bay size.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix B — Structural System for Housing The structural system consists of aluminum tube columns with a typical 4 X 6 m bay size.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix B — Structural System for Housing

segments.text: Beams are also aluminum, spaced at 2 m on center.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix B — Structural System for Housing Beams are also aluminum, spaced at 2 m on center.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix B — Structural System for Housing

segments.text: Beams and columns have fixed connections to form rigid boxes, allowing them to span up to 6 m.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix B — Structural System for Housing Beams and columns have fixed connections to form rigid boxes, allowing them to span up to 6 m.

segments.text: AGRICULTURE
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture AGRICULTURE
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: The agricultural system is derived from standard nutritional requirements for adult men and women and for children.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture The agricultural system is derived from standard nutritional requirements for adult men and women and for children.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: The space colony population is used to normalize these requirements to that of a "typical" person weighing 60 kg as shown in table 5-16.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture The space colony population is used to normalize these requirements to that of a "typical" person weighing 60 kg as shown in table 5-16.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: These requirements are met by an average daily diet which is shown in table 5-17(a) which also includes the caloric and nutritional values calculated for this diet.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture These requirements are met by an average daily diet which is shown in table 5-17(a) which also includes the caloric and nutritional values calculated for this diet.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: The nutritional requirements are met and an excess of protein is provided by a substantial margin.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture The nutritional requirements are met and an excess of protein is provided by a substantial margin.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: Vitamins and trace minerals are also available in excess quantities as shown in table 5-17(b).
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture Vitamins and trace minerals are also available in excess quantities as shown in table 5-17(b).
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: A more careful analysis of the colony's protein requirement could provide savings in meat requirements and, in turn, provide substantial savings in the required land area for plants.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture A more careful analysis of the colony's protein requirement could provide savings in meat requirements and, in turn, provide substantial savings in the required land area for plants.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: The diet is treated as a daily average' of all components as if each colonist ate a small portio~ 'of each foodstuff each day.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture The diet is treated as a daily average' of all components as if each colonist ate a small portio~ 'of each foodstuff each day.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: In reality, of course, the colonists would eat a varied selection that over time averages to this diet.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture In reality, of course, the colonists would eat a varied selection that over time averages to this diet.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: The individual components of the diet are chosen to provide adequate variety for both nutritional and psychological purposes.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture The individual components of the diet are chosen to provide adequate variety for both nutritional and psychological purposes.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: These components are meant to be representative of classes of foods and not specifically limited to these items. For example, pork could be considered as a feasible diet component with feed and area requirements intermediate between beef and rabbits.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture These components are meant to be representative of classes of foods and not specifically limited to these items. For example, pork could be considered as a feasible diet component with feed and area requirements intermediate between beef and rabbits.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: In addition, it should be explicitly stated that this diet represents typical American preferences and does not recognize ethnic or religious dietary preferences.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture In addition, it should be explicitly stated that this diet represents typical American preferences and does not recognize ethnic or religious dietary preferences.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.text: It is reasonable to expect, however, that such preferences could be adopted if desired.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture It is reasonable to expect, however, that such preferences could be adopted if desired.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix C — Agriculture

segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: There are three mechanisms that are important in mass shielding.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding There are three mechanisms that are important in mass shielding.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: First, a charged particle excites electrons for many hundreds of angstroms about its trajectory.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding First, a charged particle excites electrons for many hundreds of angstroms about its trajectory.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: This excitation extracts kinetic energy at a roughly constant rate for relativistic particles and acts as a braking mechanism.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding This excitation extracts kinetic energy at a roughly constant rate for relativistic particles and acts as a braking mechanism.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: For relativistic protons in low-Z matter this "linear energy transfer" is 2 MeV/g-cm-2 of matter.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding For relativistic protons in low-Z matter this "linear energy transfer" is 2 MeV/g-cm-2 of matter.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: If the thickness of the mass shield is great enough a particle of finite kinetic energy is stopped.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding If the thickness of the mass shield is great enough a particle of finite kinetic energy is stopped.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: This is the least effective shielding mechanism in matter for relativistic particles.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding This is the least effective shielding mechanism in matter for relativistic particles.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: The second mechanism is nuclear attenuation.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding The second mechanism is nuclear attenuation.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: For silicon dioxide the average nuclear cross section is 0.4 barn (10-24 cm2).
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding For silicon dioxide the average nuclear cross section is 0.4 barn (10-24 cm2).
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: Thus if a charged particle traverses far enough in the shield (composed of silicon dioxide) it collides with a nucleus and loses energy by inelastic collisions with the nuclear matter.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding Thus if a charged particle traverses far enough in the shield (composed of silicon dioxide) it collides with a nucleus and loses energy by inelastic collisions with the nuclear matter.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: The measure of how far a particle must travel to have a substantial chance of nuclear collision is the mean free path, which for silicon dioxide is 106 g/ cm2.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding The measure of how far a particle must travel to have a substantial chance of nuclear collision is the mean free path, which for silicon dioxide is 106 g/ cm2.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: This mechanism is an exponential damper of primary beam particles.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding This mechanism is an exponential damper of primary beam particles.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: Opposing the beam clearing tendency of nuclear attenuation is the creation of energetic secondary particles.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding Opposing the beam clearing tendency of nuclear attenuation is the creation of energetic secondary particles.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: For each nuclear collision there is beam loss from nuclear excitation, and beam enhancement (though with overall energy degradation through the increase of entropy) from the secondaries emitted by the excited nuclei.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding For each nuclear collision there is beam loss from nuclear excitation, and beam enhancement (though with overall energy degradation through the increase of entropy) from the secondaries emitted by the excited nuclei.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: These secondary particles are, of course, attenuated themselves by further nuclear collisions with roughly the same mean free path as the primary particles.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding These secondary particles are, of course, attenuated themselves by further nuclear collisions with roughly the same mean free path as the primary particles.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: The calculation of a mass shield can only be properly done by Monte Carlo simulation of the various pathways that the interactions can take.
segments.search_text: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding The calculation of a mass shield can only be properly done by Monte Carlo simulation of the various pathways that the interactions can take.
segments.heading_context: 5. A Tour of the Colony / Appendix E — Mass Shielding

segments.text: Two approximations often used either assume that secondary particles supplement nuclear attenuation well enough that only electron excitation stops the beam (the "ionization" approximation); or that secondary particle creation is negligible, resulting in beam attenuation by both nuclear attenuation and electron excitation ("ionization + exponential" approximation).
segments.search_text: 5. segments.text: Some Other Energy-Related Benefits
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits Some Other Energy-Related Benefits
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: While electricity from space and lower costs of electricity to U.S. consumers may be extremely desirable and sufficient to justify a space colonization program, there are other benefits that have not been fully evaluated in the study but may be significant.
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits While electricity from space and lower costs of electricity to U.S. consumers may be extremely desirable and sufficient to justify a space colonization program, there are other benefits that have not been fully evaluated in the study but may be significant.
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: Environmentally, microwave transmission of power from space for conversion into electricity at Earth, is a very clean form of energy production (see appendix H).
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits Environmentally, microwave transmission of power from space for conversion into electricity at Earth, is a very clean form of energy production (see appendix H).
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: It avoids emission of pollutants into the Earth's atmosphere and minimizes the waste heat introduced into the terrestrial environment.
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits It avoids emission of pollutants into the Earth's atmosphere and minimizes the waste heat introduced into the terrestrial environment.
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: The conversion of microwave energy to electricity is far more efficient than any thermodynamic process - 85 percent compared with a maximum of 50 percent.
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits The conversion of microwave energy to electricity is far more efficient than any thermodynamic process - 85 percent compared with a maximum of 50 percent.
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits 155
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: Electrical energy from space may also be the only way in which the nation can become energy independent within the same time scale of 70 years, for nNot only can it supply the needed quantities of electrical energy but also inexpensive electrical energy that might be used for electrolysis of water to produce transportable fuels and thereby reduce dependence on petroleum products in transportation systems.

segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: Another subtle energy-related benefit is the widespread nature of its application to mankind.
segments.search_text: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits Another subtle energy-related benefit is the widespread nature of its application to mankind.
segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: Low-income people spend a comparatively greater percentage of their income on electricity than do affluent people.

segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: Thus lower priced electricity would benefit an enormous number of people and not just a few.

segments.heading_context: 6. Building the Colony and Making It Prosper / Some Other Energy-Related Benefits

segments.text: This benefit from space colonization offers the potential of reaching vast numbers of people in the U.S. and providing relatively lowcost energy to many more in the developing nations of the world.

segments.description: TABLE 6-12. — COSTS AND BENEFITS OF A PROGRAM OF SPACE COLONIZATION IN 1975 DOLLARS¹ Table panel prints columns (1)–(9), years 1–45. Column (5) shows (1,0) at year 23, a downward arrow, (2,0) at year 29, a downward arrow, then (1,1) at year 43 and (2,1) at years 44–45; intermediate cells are blank in print. The source printed costs in column (2) are 0 for years 23–45. Footnote 1: The analysis runs for 70 yr. The numbers for the last 25 yr corresponding to table 6-12 are not given. They may, however, be calculated by the reader if desired. All of the required data are given within this chapter. Footnote 2: Indicates columnar numbers referred to in text. Footnote 3: These costs are obtained by summing the costs in table 6-9. Footnote 4: All learn curves with respect to SSPS’s, colonies, and chemical processing and fabricating plants, have the first unit given in the table as the second unit in a learning curve since one colony, one SSPS, and one plant were produced previously and have their costs accounted for as part of the adjusted costs of figure 6-2. Footnote 5: Second and later colonies which are finished in year X are assumed to provide their full complement of labor in year X-1. The first colony is assumed to be complete except for 37.5 percent of its radiation shield by the beginning of year 20. The colony is then slowly occupied. One-sixth of its full complement of export labor being available in year 20, one-half in year 21, five-sixths in year 22, and all of it thereafter. By the beginning of year 23 the colony has been completed. Footnote 6: The initial SSPS dollar costs can be divided into a constant cost of $2.48 billion and a variable cost of $7.26 billion. The introduction of the second-generation shuttle system reduces these numbers to 1.99 and 4.77, respectively.
